description: An animated, tileable ocean patch for a water plane. A detail wrangle picks the waves once: a main swell of wave_length running with the wind, three more swells around it and sixteen short, choppy waves on top (0.27 to 0.4 wave_length long, with most of the steepness), each a whole number of waves across the patch (the way an FFT ocean tile is built, so copies of the patch join without a seam), their heights adding up to wave_height; waves shorter than eight vertex spacings fade out (gone below four), so the grid never aliases them. A point wrangle moves them with time (deep-water speeds) as Gerstner waves whose crests choppiness pulls together, while every vertex stays on the regular grid (it solves for the wave that lands on it), so the patch stays exactly size by size; it writes exact normals, a foam value 0..1 where the swells squeeze their crests together, broken up by the chop, and a colour from deep blue-green troughs to paler, greener crests. Texture nodes make the water material from it (1024 x 1024 maps over the uv, all tileable): the colour baked into the base colour map with the foam laid over it in white, frayed at its edges by a fixed noise grain; roughness 0.2 on the water and 0.6 on the foam; and a normal map of 1.5 m ripples drifting with the wind, finer than the grid can carry, which break the glint of the light into sparkles. The render shows nine copies of the patch side by side.

wave_height.desc: height of the largest swells above sea level (m); no point rises or sinks further

wave_length.desc: distance between the largest swells (m), rounded so whole swells fit across the patch (at most size)

choppiness.desc: how sharp the crests are: 0 round swells, 1 peaked crests with plenty of foam

wind_direction.desc: where the waves run to (degrees counter-clockwise from +X, seen from above)

vertex_spacing.desc: distance between the surface's vertices (m); a patch has at most 400 x 400 quads, so a large patch with a fine spacing gets coarser

seed.desc: random seed of the waves' directions, lengths and phases (the sea state stays)

params.names: kx kz amp omega phase hx hz

water_color.note: the colour in uv space (1024 x 1024 over the patch), for the water material's base colour map

water_soft.note: smooths the colour's per-triangle steps (about one quad wide) so crests and foam have no saw-tooth edges; tileable, so the map still tiles

foam_mask.note: the foam point attribute in uv space, to lay the foam into the colour map and the roughness

foam_grain.note: a 2 m grain that frays the foam's edges; it stays put while the crests run through it, as foam stays on the water

foam_lace.note: foam + grain above 0.95 turns white (fully at 1.5): solid foam on the steepest crests, lace at its edges

water_foam.note: the foam over the water colour (screen: towards white by the foam mask)

ripples.note: 1.5 m ripples for the normal map: finer than the grid can carry, they break the glint of the light into sparkles; they drift with the wind at about their own speed (one 1.5 m cell a second)

ripple_normal.note: ripples 25 cm deep, calmer below a 1 m wave_height

params.label: size
params.expr: abs(bbox.min.x + size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.max.x - size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.min.z + size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.max.z - size / 2) < 0.001

surface.label: Ocean surface
surface.description: The water surface at the current frame: a size x size grid centred on the origin at sea level (y = 0), tileable, with uv, normals and a point foam value 0..1, in the water material (base colour map baked from the waves: deep blue-green, paler crests, white foam; roughness map: glossy water, matte foam; normal map of small ripples).
